summary: Modern databases and data platforms increasingly embed AI/ML capabilities directly where data lives, eliminating the need for separate vector stores and model-serving infrastructure. Capabilities range from in-database LLM access (text generation, summarization, embeddings) to native vector indexing for semantic search and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG). The vector database market is projected to reach USD 17.91 billion by 2034 at a ~24% CAGR, reflecting rapid enterprise adoption of vector-based retrieval for GenAI applications.

databases.name: Snowflake (Cortex AI)
databases.ai_feature: Snowflake Cortex AI (LLM functions, Cortex Search, Cortex Analyst, Document AI)
databases.description: Cortex AI provides serverless, SQL- and Python-accessible functions for LLM tasks (COMPLETE, SUMMARIZE, TRANSLATE, SENTIMENT, EXTRACT_ANSWER), embeddings, and Cortex Search for semantic/RAG retrieval. Cortex Analyst enables natural-language-to-SQL, and the platform now extends to Snowflake Postgres for unifying transactional data with analytics and AI on one governed platform.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. Snowflake provides a native VECTOR data type and VECTOR_L2_DISTANCE / VECTOR_COSINE_SIMILARITY functions, plus Cortex Search as a managed hybrid (vector + keyword) retrieval service.
databases.llm_integration: Built-in hosted LLMs (e.g., Anthropic Claude, Meta Llama, Mistral, Snowflake Arctic) accessible via SQL/Python Cortex functions; no external API keys required.
databases.pricing_notes: Consumption-based, billed in Snowflake credits by tokens processed or compute consumed; Cortex functions metered per-token, Cortex Search metered on serving/indexing compute.

databases.name: Google BigQuery (BigQuery ML + Vertex AI)
databases.ai_feature: BigQuery ML with Vertex AI integration (ML.GENERATE_TEXT, ML.GENERATE_EMBEDDING, remote models)
databases.description: BigQuery ML lets analysts create and run ML models using SQL directly in the warehouse, including classification, regression, forecasting, and clustering. Through remote models it integrates Vertex AI foundation models (Gemini) for text generation and embeddings, and supports vector search over embeddings for RAG.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. BigQuery supports a VECTOR_SEARCH function and CREATE VECTOR INDEX for approximate nearest-neighbor search over embedding columns.
databases.llm_integration: Native integration with Vertex AI (Gemini family) via remote models invoked through SQL functions like ML.GENERATE_TEXT and ML.GENERATE_EMBEDDING.
databases.pricing_notes: BigQuery ML billed on bytes processed or slot/compute; generative functions incur additional Vertex AI model charges per token/request.

databases.name: PostgreSQL (pgvector + pgai)
databases.ai_feature: pgvector extension for vector storage/search; pgai extension for in-database embeddings and LLM calls
databases.description: PostgreSQL offers mature transactions and broad driver/ORM support. The pgvector extension adds a vector column type with similarity operators, while pgai (from Timescale) adds SQL helpers to generate embeddings and call LLM providers from within the database, enabling RAG without leaving Postgres.
databases.vector_search_notes: Not native to core PostgreSQL. Vector search is provided only via the third-party pgvector extension (with HNSW and IVFFlat indexes); pgvectorscale and pgai further extend functionality. Core Postgres has no built-in vector type.
databases.llm_integration: Not built into core Postgres; the pgai extension enables calling external LLM/embedding providers (OpenAI, Ollama, Anthropic, etc.) via SQL functions.
databases.pricing_notes: Open source and free; costs depend on self-hosted infrastructure or managed provider (e.g., Timescale, Supabase, RDS) plus any external LLM API usage.

databases.name: Amazon Aurora ML
databases.ai_feature: Aurora Machine Learning (SQL integration with Amazon SageMaker, Bedrock, and Comprehend)
databases.description: Aurora ML lets you invoke ML models directly from SQL queries, passing row data to Amazon SageMaker (custom models), Amazon Bedrock (foundation/LLM models), and Amazon Comprehend (sentiment/NLP). This brings inference and generative AI into transactional queries without building separate pipelines.
databases.vector_search_notes: Aurora ML itself does not provide vector search. Aurora PostgreSQL-Compatible Edition supports vector search only through the pgvector extension, which is a separate capability from Aurora ML; Aurora ML is purely a model-invocation integration.
databases.llm_integration: Integrates with Amazon Bedrock foundation models and SageMaker-hosted LLMs, callable via SQL functions within Aurora queries.
databases.pricing_notes: No extra Aurora ML charge beyond standard Aurora compute/storage; you pay separately for the invoked SageMaker, Bedrock, or Comprehend services.

databases.name: Amazon Redshift ML
databases.ai_feature: Redshift ML (SQL-based model creation and inference via Amazon SageMaker; Bedrock LLM integration)
databases.description: Redshift ML enables data analysts to create, train, and deploy ML models using standard SQL (CREATE MODEL), with training delegated to Amazon SageMaker Autopilot. It supports in-database inference and integrates with Amazon Bedrock for generative AI / LLM use cases directly from the warehouse.
databases.vector_search_notes: Redshift ML does not provide native vector search. Amazon Redshift has introduced broader vector capabilities, but the Redshift ML service itself is focused on model training/inference, not vector similarity indexing.
databases.llm_integration: Integrates with Amazon Bedrock foundation models (and SageMaker JumpStart LLMs) invoked through SQL for generative and embedding tasks.
databases.pricing_notes: Billed on Redshift compute; model training uses SageMaker resources charged separately, and Bedrock LLM calls incur their own per-token/request costs.

databases.name: Databricks (Mosaic AI + Vector Search)
databases.ai_feature: Mosaic AI (model training/serving, agent framework) and Databricks Vector Search
databases.description: Databricks provides Mosaic AI for building, fine-tuning, and serving models and GenAI agents on the lakehouse, including foundation model APIs and governance via Unity Catalog. Databricks Vector Search offers a managed, serverless vector index automatically synced with Delta tables for RAG.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. Databricks Vector Search is a built-in managed vector database that keeps embeddings in sync with source Delta tables and supports hybrid (keyword + vector) search.
databases.llm_integration: Mosaic AI Model Serving provides Foundation Model APIs (e.g., Llama, DBRX, and external models like OpenAI/Anthropic) plus fine-tuning and an agent framework, all governed by Unity Catalog.
databases.pricing_notes: Consumption-based using Databricks Units (DBUs) for serving/compute; Vector Search and Foundation Model APIs billed by compute and tokens/requests.

databases.name: MongoDB Atlas Vector Search
databases.ai_feature: Atlas Vector Search (native vector indexing and semantic search within the document database)
databases.description: MongoDB Atlas Vector Search lets you store embeddings alongside operational JSON documents and run semantic / approximate nearest-neighbor queries using the $vectorSearch aggregation stage. It supports hybrid search and powers RAG by combining operational data, metadata filters, and vectors in one database.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. Atlas Vector Search is built into Atlas with a dedicated vector index type and the $vectorSearch operator supporting HNSW-based ANN and metadata pre-filtering.
databases.llm_integration: No built-in hosted LLMs; integrates with external providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, AWS Bedrock, Vertex AI) and frameworks like LangChain/LlamaIndex for embedding generation and RAG pipelines.
databases.pricing_notes: Included with Atlas; vector search runs on Atlas Search nodes (dedicated or shared cluster resources) billed as part of cluster/compute consumption.
